away.name: Colten Ellis
away.news: With Alex Lyon (upper body) still out this season, the Sabres have leaned heavily on Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, but they will turn to Ellis for back-to-back starts on Thursday. The 26-year-old Ellis earned another start after a tremendous performance in Buffalo's previous game, stopping all 23 shots in a 2-0 shutout win over the San Jose Sharks. The Sabres enter Thursday's action as -131 road favourites against a struggling Anaheim Ducks team that has lost six of their last seven games (1-5-1).

home.name: Ville Husso
home.news: Husso led the Ducks onto the ice for warmups.

away.name: Jonas Johansson
away.news: With Linus Ullmark (lower body) expected to miss another week, the Senators will continue to roll with Samuel Ersson and Jonas Johansson, turning to Johansson on Thursday against the Los Angeles Kings. The 31-year-old Johansson was solid in Ottawa's previous game, saving 25 of 27 shots (.926 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. The Senators enter Thursday's game as -116 road favourites against a low-scoring Kings team that scored fewer than two goals in six of their last nine games (3-5-1).

home.name: Darcy Kuemper
home.news: Kuemper had a forgettable season debut, allowing eight goals on 29 shots (.724 SV%) in an 8-4 loss to the Colorado Avalanche, but has been solid since. The 36-year-old veteran goalie has won three straight games, posting a 2.26 GAA and .931 SV%. Still, the Kings enter Thursday's game as slight +105 home underdogs against an Ottawa Senators team that has lost three of their last five games (2-3-0).

away.name: Leevi Merilainen
away.news: Leevi Merilainen has struggled in recent games, but he will return to the crease for a third straight outing, an unfortunate testament to his counterpart, Kevin Lankinen's abysmal play. The 24-year-old Merilainen remains the preferred choice in Vancouver's crease, despite allowing 14 goals on 100 shots (.860 SV%) in his past three games (1-2-0). Merilainen has a 3.35 GAA and a .900 SV% in nine appearances this season (2-3-1). The Canucks enter Thursday's outing as +148 road underdogs against a San Jose Sharks team coming off a 2-0 loss to the Buffalo Sabres.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov started the season with a dreadful 4.00 GAA and .848 SV% in his first five games (2-3-0), but has turned things around in recent outings. Despite a 1-2-0 record, Askarov has been stellar in his last three games, allowing two or fewer goals in each and saving 109 of 114 combined shots (.956 SV%). The Sharks enter Thursday's game as -165 home favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team coming off an impressive come-from-behind 6-5 overtime win over the Anaheim Ducks.
